answer: An ambition I have held for many years is to one day start my own business. I first had this dream as a teenager, watching my father run his small enterprise with such dedication. He ran that business for over thirty years before retiring recently, and I saw both the freedom and the worry it brought him. What has always appealed to me is the idea of building something of my own and being [[self-reliant]]. More specifically, I would love to open my own education consultancy in Sirajganj, so that students here would not have to travel to Dhaka for reliable advice. Towards this goal, I have been gaining relevant work experience and quietly saving whatever I can. My current job has taught me how the whole process works, from counselling students to dealing with universities and visa requirements. I am also constantly learning about how businesses operate, since I know success requires far more than just a good idea. This ambition matters to me because it represents freedom, creativity and the chance to make a real impact. Honestly, I find the idea both thrilling and slightly [[daunting]], given the risks involved. Still, I believe the potential rewards, both financial and personal, are worth it. My father always says that a business is like a child, needing constant care, and I think he is right. I know it will require enormous [[perseverance]], but it is a dream I refuse to let go of. With my father's [[hard-earned]] advice and enough preparation, I am confident that one day I will make it happen and prove myself as a genuinely [[entrepreneurial]] person.

followUps.q: Would you ask your father to help with your business?
followUps.answer: Definitely, at least as an adviser. He knows a great deal about managing money, dealing with customers and surviving difficult years, which is exactly the kind of practical wisdom no textbook can give you.

followUps.q: Do many young people in your country want to start a business?
followUps.answer: More and more, I think. Many young graduates are frustrated by limited job opportunities, so they start small online businesses. Social media has made it much easier to get started with very little [[capital]].

note: Father 'ran' the business and has retired (persona); made the ambition concrete (own consultancy in Sirajganj) and added what his job has taught him; plain 'impact' unmarked, added [[hard-earned]] and [[entrepreneurial]].
